subject: Logic
title: Appeal to Authority
description: A quick, practical guide to Appeal to Authority.

hook.text: A famous physicist endorses a brand of shoes. Should you trust the recommendation?

buildup.text: Appeal to authority uses someone's status, not evidence, to support a claim.

discovery.text: Expert opinion matters—but only within their field. A physicist isn't a shoe expert.

twist.text: Even real experts can be wrong. Authority strengthens an argument but never replaces evidence.

climax.text: Ask: is this person an expert in this specific topic? Is there data backing their claim?

quiz.question: When is an appeal to authority fallacious?
options: When the expert is in the relevant field
When the authority is outside their expertise
